name: mlview
description: Visualize and audit Python ML pipelines as an interactive diagram — fully local, static analysis only.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Analysis spawns a Python interpreter, so it is disabled in Restricted Mode. Trust the workspace to enable MLView.

virtualWorkspaces.description: MLView runs a local Python interpreter over files on disk.

commands.title: Save Current Graph As Comparison Base

mlview.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the Python interpreter used to run the MLView analyzer. Leave empty to use the Python extension's active interpreter, `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, or a `PATH` probe, in that order.

mlview.analyzeOnSave.description: Re-analyze (debounced by 400 ms) when a Python file in the workspace is saved.

enumDescriptions: Analyze only the file itself. Fastest, and the least accurate: the cross-file rules (MLV301, MLV302, MLV401, MLV501) cannot fire, and the analyzer reports that as a single_file_analysis diagnostic.
Analyze the package directory that contains the file, then scope the diagram to the file. Recovers the cross-file rules at a fraction of workspace cost.
Analyze the whole workspace, then scope the diagram to the file.
mlview.currentFileAnalysisScope.markdownDescription: What `MLView: Visualize (Current File)` actually analyzes. `package` (default) analyzes the outermost directory of the package chain containing the file (the file's own directory when it is not in a package) and then scopes the diagram to the file, so the cross-file rules still fire. `file` analyzes the file alone and is reported as incomplete.

mlview.exclude.markdownDescription:
Extra glob patterns excluded from discovery. Added to the analyzer defaults (.venv, site-packages, node_modules, build, .git).

**Precedence:** this setting is an ADDITIVE filter. `[paths].exclude` in the configuration file `#mlview.configPath#` names WINS; these globs drop further paths on top of it and cannot re-include a path the file excluded.

mlview.configPath.markdownDescription:
Path to the `.mlview.toml` (or a `pyproject.toml` carrying a `[tool.mlview]` table) MLView passes to `--config`. Absolute, or relative to the workspace folder. Leave empty to discover `<folder>/.mlview.toml`, then `<folder>/pyproject.toml` when it has the table.

**Precedence:** the file WINS for `[rules].disable` and `[paths].exclude`. `#mlview.disabledRules#` and `#mlview.exclude#` are ADDITIVE filters on top of it - they can hide more rules and drop more paths, but neither can re-enable a rule the file disabled or re-include a path it excluded.

mlview.baselinePath.markdownDescription:
Path to a baseline written by **MLView: Create Baseline From Current Findings** (`mlview baseline write`). Findings recorded in it are still shown, but stop counting - so a repository with pre-existing findings can adopt MLView without `--fail-on high` failing forever. Absolute, or relative to the workspace folder. Empty means no baseline, and one is never auto-discovered: a file that quietly empties the Problems panel has to be named here on purpose.

**Precedence:** the same as `#mlview.configPath#` - a `[baseline]` table in the configuration file wins, and this setting only names the file when the TOML does not.

mlview.includeNotebooks.description: Analyze .ipynb notebooks as well as .py files (passes --include-notebooks). Off by default: cell execution order cannot be recovered from the file, so order-sensitive findings inside a notebook are de-rated and reported as such.

mlview.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of Python files to discover.

mlview.maxNodes.description: Maximum number of graph nodes. Exceeding it truncates the graph and shows a banner.

mlview.minSeverity.description: Lowest issue severity shown in the Problems panel and in the chat / language-model digests.

mlview.minConfidence.description: Lowest issue confidence published as a diagnostic. Lower-confidence findings stay on the canvas only.

mlview.diagnosticsEnabled.description: Publish MLView findings to the Problems panel. This is the surface GitHub Copilot reads via #problems.

mlview.diagnosticSeverity.markdownDescription: How high-severity findings map into the Problems panel. `warning` (default) publishes them as warnings; `error` escalates them to errors. Medium is always a warning and low is always information.

mlview.disabledRules.markdownDescription:
Rule codes to hide everywhere: the Problems panel, the issue quick pick, the diagram and the chat / language-model digests. Example: MLV601.

**Precedence:** this setting is an ADDITIVE filter. `[rules].disable` in the configuration file `#mlview.configPath#` names WINS; these codes hide further rules on top of it and cannot re-enable a rule the file disabled.

mlview.codeLens.description: Show a "MLView: show in diagram" CodeLens above analyzed units.

mlview.trace.description: Verbosity of the MLView output channel.

languageModelTools.name: mlview_analyzeWorkspace
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Statically analyze the Python ML code in the workspace (or one file) and return the pipeline structure: stages, connections, frameworks, and a summary of detected issues with file and line numbers. Does not execute the user's code. Use before answering questions about how training or evaluation is wired together.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Analyze the ML workflow in this workspace

path.description: Optional workspace-relative file or folder; defaults to the whole workspace.

scope.description: Optional CONTRACTS.md 11.1 diagram selector. Omit it for the whole graph, or pass one of -- "all" the whole graph, spelled explicitly. "stage:<id>" one lane: config, data, preprocess, model, objective, train, eval or deliver. "unit:<name>" one class, function or loop -- a qualname ("train.train"), a bare name ("SmallCNN") or a node id. Resolves to every match, and says when it is ambiguous. "file:<path.py>" everything the analyzer found in one file (workspace-relative, forward slashes, or a basename). "concern:<name>" config | data | optimization | evaluation -- the four presets that partition the eight stages (aliases: setup, preprocessing, dataset, training, inference). "node:<nodeId>" one node and its neighbourhood. "symbol:<name>" an alias for "unit:<name>". A scope outside this grammar (including a stage id outside the eight canonical stages, a concern that is not one of the four, or a node id this graph does not contain) comes back as an error naming the accepted values -- never as a silently substituted default. Every scoped result says it is a filtered view: its counts describe the scope, not the project.

depth.description: 0, 1 or 2 boundary hops around the scope. Omit it for the per-kind default: 1 for unit/node (a point, so its interface is the answer), 0 for stage/file/concern (already a region). Ignored without a scope.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with MLView
walkthroughs.description: Draw the ML pipeline in this workspace, then read what the analyzer found - in five steps.

steps.title: Install the MLView analyzer
steps.description:
MLView draws; `python -m mlview` analyzes. Point the extension at an interpreter that has it.
[Select Python Interpreter](command:mlview.selectInterpreter)

steps.title: Visualize a pipeline
steps.description:
Open the bundled sample (or any workspace with Python in it) and draw the whole workflow.
[Visualize ML Workflow (Workspace)](command:mlview.visualizeWorkspace)

steps.title: Read a finding in Problems
steps.description:
Every finding is a diagnostic with a rule code, a fix hint and an offline rule page.
[Show ML Issues](command:mlview.showIssues)

steps.title: Jump from the editor to the diagram
steps.description:
Alt+M takes the cursor to the node it belongs to, without leaving the keyboard.
[Reveal in Diagram (Alt+M)](command:mlview.revealInDiagram)

media.altText: Jump from the editor to the diagram

steps.title: Narrow the diagram to one unit
steps.description:
Alt+Shift+M scopes the diagram to the enclosing class, function or loop - and says how many findings are outside it.
[Scope Diagram to Symbol (Alt+Shift+M)](command:mlview.scopeToSymbol)

media.altText: Narrow the diagram to one unit
